guidelineReference: Resus Council UK Paediatric Basic Life Support 2021 (Choking)
title: Infant choking at a community festival
setting: Eid in the park event. A frantic parent runs in holding an 8-month-old infant who is choking on a plastic button. Red face, unable to cry.
verdictExplanation: Severe complete paediatric airway obstruction in an infant (unable to cry, cough, or breathe). Choking is a critical life-threatening emergency. Sick: deliver infant choking treatment.

shared.response: Responding only to touch with panicked movements
shared.circulation: Skin is red and puffy, cyanosis around lips

history.history: Tripped and managed to get a button off his jacket, choked on it 2 minutes ago

followUp.question: What is the correct treatment sequence for an infant with severe choking?

options.text: Give up to 5 back blows (head down, supported on lap), then up to 5 chest thrusts; repeat
Give up to 5 back blows followed by up to 5 abdominal thrusts
Perform a blind finger sweep to hook the button out immediately
Perform adult CPR (30 chest compressions) starting with compressions

followUp.explanation: Infant choking. Give up to 5 back blows (head down, supported on your thigh/forearm). If unsuccessful, give up to 5 chest thrusts (using two fingers on the chest). Never perform abdominal thrusts in infants (under 1 year) due to risk of liver damage. Finger sweeps are contraindicated.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999 immediately. Deliver 5 back blows, then 5 chest thrusts. Reassure parents.
levelFlags.erNotes: Manage infant choking. If infant loses consciousness, immediately guide to floor, call 999, and start CPR (beginning with 5 rescue breaths, check mouth before breathing).
